question: is the paired minimum detectable effect still a meaningful design target once the instrument is allowed to vary
method: coverage was computed for each of the eight confirmation artifacts under both scoring methods, and the per-artifact difference was treated as an instrument facet
finding: the instrument does not merely shift the endpoint, it varies. The standard deviation of the method difference across artifacts is 0.301, about 3.65 times the minimum detectable effect the design was sized for, and the variance of the method difference is 1.48 times the variance of the coverage it is measuring. The difference also changes sign, from -0.167 to +0.667, so it cannot be removed as a constant offset.

consequence.mde_void_as_a_design_target: the paired minimum detectable effect of 0.0825 was computed with the instrument treated as fixed. It omits a variance component larger than the one it used, so it cannot be used to size a block.
consequence.what_is_needed: sample-size planning must treat the scoring method as a facet with its own variance, in the way generalizability designs do, rather than as a settled choice made before the study
consequence.not_a_correction: because the difference changes sign across artifacts, no constant adjustment recovers the earlier number

limits: eight artifacts on two tasks, one repeat each
one judge for the whole-artifact path
coverage here is a six-element proportion, so single element flips move it by 0.167
claim_scope: design validity evidence only; no treatment effect is claimed
